'''Johnnie To Kei-fung''' (born 22 April 1955) is a Hong Kong filmmaker, best known for his [[Hong Kong action cinema|action]] and [[crime film|crime]] movies, including ''[[The Mission (1999 film)|The Mission]]'' (1999), ''[[PTU (film)|PTU]]'' (2003), ''[[Breaking News (2004 film)|Breaking News]]'' (2004), ''[[Election (2005 film)|Election]]'' (2005), ''[[Election 2]]'' and ''[[Exiled (2006 film)|Exiled]]'' (both 2006), and ''[[Drug War (film)|Drug War]]'' (2012). His films, often made in collaboration with the same group of actors, screenwriters and cinematographers, tend to explore themes of friendship, fate and the changing face of Hong Kong society.<ref name="Cineaste: Interview with Johnnie To">{{cite web |last=Nochimson |first=Martha P. |last2=Cashill |first2=Robert |date=Spring 2007 |title=One Country, Two Visions: An Interview with Johnnie To |url=http://www.cineaste.com/articles/an-interview-with-johnnie-to.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130101072228/http://www.cineaste.com/articles/an-interview-with-johnnie-to.htm |archive-date=2013-01-01 |access-date=2013-02-18 |website=[[Cinéaste (magazine)|Cinéaste]]}}</ref><ref name="fredcamper.com">{{cite web |last=Camper |first=Fred |date=2007-09-07 |title=Review of Exiled for the Chicago Reader, by Fred Camper |url=http://www.fredcamper.com/Film/To.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120715014449/http://www.fredcamper.com/Film/To.html |archive-date=2012-07-15 |access-date=2013-02-18 |publisher=Fredcamper.com}}</ref> He co-founded the production company [[Milkyway Image]] with his frequent co-director [[Wai Ka-fai]]. 

==Career==
To began his career at age 17 as a messenger for the Hong Kong television studio [[TVB]].<ref name="Green Cine: Johnnie To">{{cite web |last=Axmaker |first=Sean |date=2004-02-19 |title=Karma Chameleon: A Talk with Johnnie To |url=http://www.greencine.com/article?action=view&articleID=111 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120211080342/http://www.greencine.com/article?action=view&articleID=111 |archive-date=2012-02-11 |access-date=2013-02-18 |website=[[GreenCine]]}}</ref> From there To moved up the ladder, working as an executive producer and director for TV shows starting in 1973. In 1978, he shot his first theatrical feature, but continued working in television. In 1983, he directed and screen-wrote the critically acclaimed ''[[The Legend of the Condor Heroes (1983 TV series)|The Legend of the Condor Heroes]]'', a dramatised TV series based on [[The Legend of the Condor Heroes|the martial art novel of the same name]] by [[Jin Yong]].

While working as an assistant TV director during the [[Shaw Studios]] era he directed ''[[All About Ah-Long]]'' (1989), starring [[Chow Yun-fat]]. The film became one of the biggest box office hits that year. In 1988, he co-directed ''[[The Big Heat (1988 film)|The Big Heat]]'', his first [[action movie]]. The film was produced by [[Tsui Hark]]. The end of the 1980s also saw some of To's biggest commercial successes, the vast majority of which were comedies. His 1988 film ''[[The Eighth Happiness]]'' was that year's highest-grossing movie.<ref>{{cite web |last=Vidouze |first=David-Olivier |date=March 2000 |title=Johnnie To Kei Fung |url=http://www.hkcinemagic.com/en/people.asp?id=143 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110513100149/http://www.hkcinemagic.com/en/people.asp?id=143 |archive-date=2011-05-13 |access-date=2013-02-18 |website=[[Hong Kong Cinemagic]]}}</ref>

In 1996, To and frequent collaborator [[Wai Ka-fai]] formed [[Milkyway Image]], a production house specialising in cost-efficient [[independent film]]s made by To and Wai, as well as their frequent collaborators from [[Law Wing-cheung]] to scriptwriter [[Yau Nai-hoi]].

From 1999 to 2001, To was the chief operational officer of [[China Star Entertainment Group]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Hansen |first=Jeremy |date=2001-08-17 |title=Webfiles: 'I Want to Make Films That Belong to Me' |url=http://www.asiaweek.com/asiaweek/daily/foc/0%2C8773%2C171039%2C00.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020329130555/http://www.asiaweek.com/asiaweek/daily/foc/0,8773,171039,00.html |archive-date=2002-03-29 |access-date=2025-02-23 |magazine=[[Asiaweek]]}}</ref> To was appointed to the [[Hong Kong Arts Development Council]] in 2004 and soon after chaired its Film and Media Arts Group.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Johnnie K F To |url=https://www.hkbu.edu.hk/en/about/honorary-doctorates-and-honorary-university-fellows/johnnie-k-f-to.html |access-date=2024-05-09 |website=[[Hong Kong Baptist University]] |language=en |archive-date=2024-05-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240509063627/https://www.hkbu.edu.hk/en/about/honorary-doctorates-and-honorary-university-fellows/johnnie-k-f-to.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

To served as a jury member at the [[2011 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2011-05-05 |title=The Jury of the 64th Festival de Cannes |url=https://www.festival-cannes.com/en/2011/the-jury-of-the-64th-festival-de-cannes/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240509063625/https://www.festival-cannes.com/en/2011/the-jury-of-the-64th-festival-de-cannes/ |archive-date=2024-05-09 |access-date=2024-05-09 |website=[[Cannes Film Festival]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

His film ''[[Life Without Principle (film)|Life Without Principle]]'' (2011) was selected as the Hong Kong's entry for [[Academy Award for Best International Feature Film|Best Foreign Language Film]] at the [[85th Academy Awards]],<ref name="Oscars">{{cite news |date=2012-09-21 |title=Greece Picks ''Unfair World'' for Oscar race |url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/life-principle-chosen-as-hong-372933 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170320135739/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/life-principle-chosen-as-hong-372933 |archive-date=2017-03-20 |access-date=2012-09-21 |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref> but did not make the shortlist.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Morgan |first=David |date=2012-12-21 |title=9 Foreign Films on Oscar Shortlist |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/9-foreign-films-on-oscar-shortlist/ |access-date=2024-05-09 |website=[[CBS News]] |language=en-US}}</ref><!-- 2011-2013 term, at least-->

In 2016, To served as the Jury President for the [[10th Asian Film Awards]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shackleton |first=Liz |date=2016-02-03 |title=''The Assassin'' Leads Nods for Asian Film Awards |url=https://www.screendaily.com/the-assassin-leads-nods-for-asian-film-awards/5099757.article |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240509063625/https://www.screendaily.com/the-assassin-leads-nods-for-asian-film-awards/5099757.article |archive-date=2024-05-09 |access-date=2024-05-09 |website=[[Screen International|Screen Daily]] |language=en}}</ref>

In June 2017, To was invited to become a member of the [[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stedman |first=Alex |date=2017-06-28 |title=Academy Invites Record 774 New Members |url=https://variety.com/2017/film/news/academy-new-members-class-of-2017-1202481404/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180424220758/http://variety.com/2017/film/news/academy-new-members-class-of-2017-1202481404/ |archive-date=2018-04-24 |access-date=2024-05-09 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

In June 2019, To was announced as the Jury President for the [[56th Golden Horse Awards]], but resigned his position in September.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chu |first=Karen |date=2019-09-20 |title=Hong Kong Director Johnnie To Resigns as Golden Horse Awards Jury President Amid Beijing Boycott |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/johnnie-resigns-as-golden-horse-awards-jury-president-beijing-boycott-1241302/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220409205644/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/johnnie-resigns-as-golden-horse-awards-jury-president-beijing-boycott-1241302/ |archive-date=2022-04-09 |access-date=2024-05-09 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-09-19 |title=Wang Toon Will Succeed as New Jury President |url=https://www.goldenhorse.org.tw/news/detail/1233 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240509063626/https://www.goldenhorse.org.tw/news/detail/1233 |archive-date=2024-05-09 |access-date=2024-05-09 |website=[[Golden Horse Film Festival and Awards|Taipei Golden Horse Film Festival]] |language=zh}}</ref>

In February 2023, To served as a jury member at the [[73rd Berlin International Film Festival]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goodfellow |first=Melanie |date=2023-02-01 |title=Berlin Jury Announced; Includes Golshifteh Farahani, Johnnie To & ''12 Years A Slave'', ''Babylon'', ''She Said'' Casting Director Francine Maisler |url=https://deadline.com/2023/02/berlin-jury-2023-golshifteh-farahani-amp-johnnie-to-kristen-stewart-1235246398/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230216161038/https://deadline.com/2023/02/berlin-jury-2023-golshifteh-farahani-amp-johnnie-to-kristen-stewart-1235246398/ |archive-date=2023-02-16 |access-date=2023-02-16 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood|Deadline]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Festivals and recognition==
{{main|List of awards and nominations received by Johnnie To}}

Commercially successful in his native Hong Kong, To's films have regularly appeared at international festivals, most notably in Europe and North America. Six of To's films have been featured at the [[Cannes Film Festival]]: ''[[Breaking News (2004 film)|Breaking News]]'' (2004),<ref name="cannes-2004.com">{{cite web |title=Breaking News |url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/4196904/year/2004.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121010231853/http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/4196904/year/2004.html |archive-date=2012-10-10 |access-date=2009-12-05 |work=[[Cannes Film Festival]]}}</ref> ''[[Election (2005 film)|Election]]'' was shown in Competition in [[2005 Cannes Film Festival|2005]];<ref name="cannes-2005.com">{{cite web |title=Election |url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/4282802/year/2005.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121011042108/http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/4282802/year/2005.html |archive-date=2012-10-11 |access-date=2009-12-05 |work=[[Cannes Film Festival]]}}</ref> its sequel, ''[[Election 2]]'' (a.k.a. ''Triad Election'', 2006), ''[[Triangle (2007 film)|Triangle]]'' (2007), and ''[[Blind Detective]]'' (2013) were screened out-of-competition, while ''[[Vengeance (2009 film)|Vengeance]]'' (2009) competed for the [[Palme d'Or]]. At the [[Berlin International Film Festival]], ''[[Sparrow (2008 film)|Sparrow]]'' was shown in competition in 2008. At the [[Venice International Film Festival]], ''[[Throw Down (film)|Throw Down]]'' was screened out-of-competition in [[61st Venice International Film Festival|2004]]; ''[[Exiled (2006 film)|Exiled]]'' (2006), ''[[Mad Detective]]'' (2007) and ''[[Life Without Principle (film)|Life Without Principle]]'' (2011) were shown in competition.

In North America, To's films have been consistently screened at the [[Toronto International Film Festival]]. ''[[The Mission (1999 film)|The Mission]]'', ''[[Fulltime Killer]]'', ''[[PTU (film)|PTU]]'', ''Breaking News'', ''Throw Down'' and ''Mad Detective'' all screened between 1999 and 2007. In 2006, ''Election'', ''Election 2'', and ''Exiled'' were screened.

In 2005, To received the "Time Machine Career Achievement Award" at the [[Festival de Cine de Sitges]], Europe's most prestigious film festival specializing in genre films. To was also honoured as a "Filmmaker in Focus" of the 2007 [[International Film Festival Rotterdam]]. In 2009, while ''Vengeance'' competed at Cannes, To was made an officer of the [[Ordre des Arts et des Lettres|French Order of Arts and Letters]] by the French [[Minister of Culture (France)|Minister of Culture]] in recognition of his films.<ref>[http://www.hkadc.org.hk/en/infocentre/press/press_20090526 ADC congratulates Johnnie To awarded the Officer of the National Order of Arts and Letters by French Ministry of Culture / Press Releases / Information Centre / Hong Kong Arts Development Council] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721093952/http://www.hkadc.org.hk/en/infocentre/press/press_20090526 |date=21 July 2011 }}</ref>

The annual [[Hong Kong International Film Festival]] held its 45th edition in April 2021 and To directed a segment of the 2020 anthology film ''[[Septet: The Story of Hong Kong]]'' along with [[Sammo Hung]], [[Ann Hui]], [[Patrick Tam (film director)|Patrick Tam]], [[Tsui Hark]], [[Yuen Woo-ping]] and [[Ringo Lam]]. The short films were shot entirely on 35mm film, each of them touching on a nostalgic and moving story set across different time periods, with every one being an ode to the city.<ref>{{cite web |date=2021-04-02 |title=Must-Watch Chinese Film Premieres at the 2021 Hong Kong International Film Festival |url=https://www.igafencu.com/r/hong-kong-international-film-festival-2021/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210425152655/https://www.igafencu.com/r/hong-kong-international-film-festival-2021/ |archive-date=2021-04-25 |access-date=2021-04-25 |website=[[Gafencu Men]]}}</ref>

In 2024, To was appointed jury member at the [[37th Tokyo International Film Festival|2024 Tokyo International Film Festival]] for its section 'International competition'.<ref name="jury:hr">{{Cite web |author=Rahman |first=Abid |date=2024-08-01 |title=Tokyo Film Festival Reveals 2024 Competition Jury Members |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/tokyo-film-festival-2024-competition-jury-1235964983/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240802103224/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/tokyo-film-festival-2024-competition-jury-1235964983/ |archive-date=2024-08-02 |access-date=2024-09-08 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |lang=en}}</ref>
